title: Transient Headroom Allocator and Spillover Backpressure Calculator
author: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets must avoid brittle capacity spikes and cross-pool overload during transient surges. This PR introduces a transient headroom allocator plus a spillover backpressure calculator to improve graceful degradation and fairness when capacity is constrained.

What it does (summary):
- Adds a transient headroom allocator that computes short-term headroom budgets per-tenant using a decaying forecast window (exponential decay over 30s by default). Headroom is expressed as a prioritized budget vector (steady, burst, emergency) so we can differentiate sustained commits from true bursts.
- Implements a spillover backpressure calculator used by the gateway/router to compute an orthogonal "spill score" when a pool is near saturation; the score drives either soft-rejects or cross-pool forwarding according to policy.
- Exposes new telemetry: per-tenant utilization histograms (P50/P90/P99), headroom consumption traces, and spill events as structured logs so Optimize can recommend warm-pool sizing.
- Adds a fairness window applied to burst grants to prevent repeated micro-burst monopolization (sliding-window token decay).

Design notes: The allocator runs every 250ms and uses an internal lightweight forecaster built on EWMA+variance to avoid O(n) per-request overhead. The spillover calculator uses occupancy and recent ingress gradient to compute a probabilistic spill probability; this reduces thrashing compared to hard thresholds. Policies are pluggable so Dedicated customers can opt into strict throughput guarantees or latency-first burst modes.

Backward compatibility: Default policy preserves existing SLOs; new settings are behind a feature flag (dedicated.transientHeadroom.enabled = false by default) and do not change current autoscaler contracts unless explicitly enabled.

Testing: Unit tests for allocator math, integration test that replays synthetic burst traces against a local fleet (included), and a small load test in perf-canary which verifies 12% lower 95th percentile tail amplification during controlled bursts.

Deployment plan: Gradual rollout behind flag, staged to non-production fleets for 48h, then canary to 3 production pools, followed by full rollout if no regressions.

Related: ENG-4321 (burst fairness), ENG-4367 (spillover telemetry), incident INT-21983 noted an event where cross-pool spill generated oscillation which this PR addresses.

review_comments: Maya Chen (review): Nice separation of concerns. Question: why EWMA and not a tiny AR(1)? Can you add a short justification and link to the microbenchmarks?
Sofia Ramirez (reply): EWMA chosen for computational simplicity and bounded memory; added microbenchmarks in allocator_test.go and commentary in docs/operators/transient_headroom.md.

Arjun Patel (review): Spill probability looks promising, but I saw a small oscillation in the integration replay when combined with the existing warm-pool autoscaler. Request: add a damping term or minimum hysteresis window.
Sofia Ramirez (reply): Added a minimum hysteresis of 500ms and a damping coefficient in spillover_calculator.go; integration replay now shows stable convergence.
